title: U.S. Southwest semiconductor workforce and supplier scaling evidence
question: Can local supplier and workforce systems support semiconductor scaling?
why_it_matters: Funded semiconductor projects only become operating capacity if labor pipelines, construction capacity, suppliers, training systems, and capital commitments can keep up.
current_support: FTFN has national CHIPS context, MAG regional projections, and a named TSMC registered technician apprenticeship record identifying four technician pathways, education partners, more than $5 million of company support, an 18-to-24-month program horizon, and a target of nearly 130 apprentices and trainees in 2025.
missing_evidence: apprenticeship enrollment, completion, retention, and placement outcomes
training capacity relative to fab and supplier demand
candidate_records: MAG 2023 population, housing, and employment projections
TSMC apprenticeship outcome and retention data
Arizona occupation-specific labor and vacancy data
next_action: Add apprenticeship outcome, occupation-level labor, construction-trade, and supplier operating records before making chip-corridor workforce or supplier sufficiency claims.
notes: Phase 51B added a named facility-linked technician pipeline, but the gap remains unresolved because planned cohorts do not prove completion, retention, total labor sufficiency, construction capacity, or supplier-network maturity.
